intro: My research develops a structural theory of AI alignment: instead of treating safety as a data-scaling problem, I study alignment as a set of low-dimensional behaviors that can be recovered, controlled, and verified inside learned systems.

This agenda connects three layers of work. In reinforcement learning, I build neurosymbolic safety and multi-objective control methods that make agent behavior mathematically bounded and operator-tunable. In distillation, I show that complex behaviors can be transferred from models using only synthetic noise, revealing alignment-relevant behavior as a compact structural object. In scientific foundation models, I apply these principles through verifiable rewards so models obey physical and logical constraints by design.

objectives.title: Objective 1: Build Verifiable Control for RL Agents

blocks.title: The Problem
blocks.content: AI agents deployed in high-stakes settings cannot be trusted on empirical performance alone. A reward-maximizing policy can violate safety constraints, exploit ambiguous specifications, or behave in ways that are difficult for an operator to audit.

blocks.title: My Approach
blocks.content: I develop safe and interpretable RL systems that pair learned dynamics with formal reasoning. AutoSpec automates and visualizes behavioral specifications from imperfect user intent. SPARKD and RAMPS use weakest preconditions, Koopman-linearized dynamics, and optimization-based shielding to create provable guardrails for nonlinear environments. This turns safety from an after-the-fact evaluation into a constraint enforced during action selection. [View AutoSpec Homepage]

blocks.title: The Problem
blocks.content: Real deployments rarely optimize a single objective. Defense, robotics, energy, and scientific systems require agents to trade off safety, performance, cost, interpretability, and mission priorities as conditions change.

blocks.title: My Approach
blocks.content: Through the DoD-funded MIXTAPE initiative with Kitware, I develop multi-objective RL methods such as D3PO and ESR-PPO. These frameworks train a single policy whose reward weights can be adjusted at runtime, allowing a human operator to observe and control how changing objective priorities alter the agent's behavior without retraining.

objectives.title: Objective 3: Recover and Diagnose Alignment Structure

blocks.title: The Problem
blocks.content: Modern alignment methods often assume behavior is deeply entangled with massive training datasets. That makes safety behavior hard to isolate, transfer, or diagnose, especially when hidden failure modes are embedded inside opaque models.

blocks.title: My Approach
blocks.content: My zero-data noise distillation work tests whether behavior can be separated from the original data distribution. By training student models from teacher outputs on pure synthetic noise, I recover complex RL policies and language-model behaviors with high fidelity. The same process also exposes latent vulnerabilities, because hidden failure modes can transfer along with desired behavior. This reframes distillation as both a transfer method and a diagnostic tool for alignment.

objectives.title: Objective 4: Scale Verifiable Alignment to Scientific LLMs

blocks.title: The Problem
blocks.content: Scientific foundation models fail dangerously when they hallucinate physically impossible outputs. In domains such as chemistry, materials discovery, and engineering simulation, a model must satisfy computable constraints before its outputs can be trusted.

blocks.title: My Approach
blocks.content: I extend the same verification-driven alignment principles to scientific LLMs through Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR). In chemistry, this means rewarding mechanistic constraints such as atom balance, mass balance, charge consistency, stereochemistry, and valid reaction structure. The goal is to build domain-native models that are transparent in their failure modes and bounded by physical laws rather than only by human preference data.
